text: AI Engineering Handbook (RAG Test Document) RAG Basics RAG stands for Retrieval Augmented Generation. A RAG system retrieves relevant documents before generating an answer. Core pipeline: chunk documents, create embeddings, retrieve top results, generate answer with citations. Chunk overlap helps maintain context across document boundaries. Without retrieval grounding, language models may hallucinate.

Hybrid Retrieval BM25 is keyword-based retrieval and works well for exact terms. Vector search is semantic retrieval and works well for meaning and paraphrases. Hybrid retrieval combines BM25 and vector search. This improves recall and robustness in search results. A reranker model improves the final relevance of selected chunks.

Citation Enforcement Production AI systems must show evidence for answers. Every factual claim should be linked to a source chunk. If evidence is missing, the system should respond with 'I don't know'. Confidence scores can be estimated from retrieval and reranking. Evaluation datasets help measure system reliability.
